CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, February 28, 2024 at 7:00 pm

  FEBRUARY 2024 AGENDA

MEMBERS
Barbara Hibler, Chairperson  Peter Puglese, TE, PE, Public Works Department, City Traffic Engineer
Richard Galindo, District 1  Diana Maximo, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
Kip Rudd, District 2  William Thompson, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department
Lois Hale, District 4
Raquel Mendez, Secretary

Rules of Decorum
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/DocumentCenter/View/18857/2023-Rules-of-Decorum

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
1. Roll Call

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission (PTC) on any item on the agenda, other than the
  Public Hearing, may do so at this time.

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on January 24, 2023

D. PUBLIC HEARING
1. Staff report recommending that the PTC conduct a public hearing to do the following:
a. Receive public comments regarding the termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program on 6th Avenue
  from 104th Street to 108th Street; and
b. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

E. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. Vehicles parked from West Boulevard to Crenshaw Blvd at Manchester Boulevard
a. The vehicles in question at this location are blocking the pedestrian sidewalk. The Commission is looking for a
  solution that allows the sidewalk to have path accessible to all types of pedestrians at all time.

2. Active-Transportation-and-Safe-Routes-to-School-Plan-Adopted-May-17-2022. Report found at the following link
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/DocumentCenter/View/17698/Active-Transportation-and-Safe-Routes-to-School-Plan-Adopted-May-17-2022
a. Status of presentation on Safe Routes to School Plan

3. Ordinance Designating City-Owned Parking Facilities as Parking Meter Zones and Establishing Special Event
  Parking Rates & fine for Parking Meter Zones. Staff Report found at the following link
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/16501?fileID=23365
a. Status of the statistical report on shuttle and parking usage, especially how public use of the city's parking
  resources adapts during weekday events

F. NEW BUSINESS: NONE

G. REFERRAL FROM CITY COUNCIL OR CITY DEPARTMENT: NONE

H. PARKING AND TRAFFIC CONTROL: NONE

I.  POLICE DEPARTMENT: NONE

J. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

K. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on City related
  travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of general interest to the
  public.

L. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. The next Parking and Traffic Commission meeting will be held on Wednesday, March 27, 2024 at 7:00 p.m., First
  Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301.

M. ADJOURNMENT

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, February 28, 2024 at 7:00 pm
  JANUARY 2024 MEETING MINUTES

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
 Chairperson Hibler welcomed the commission and the public for their attendance and participation.
 Meeting was held at 7pm (PST) in the Chamber Room located in the 9th Floor on January 24, 2024
 Attendees included:
  MEMBERS  Raquel Mendez, Secretary
  Barbara Hibler, Chairperson  Victor Nunez, Public Works Operations Manager
  Richard Galindo, District 1  Diana Maximo, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
  Kip Rudd, District 2  William Thompson, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
  Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department
  Lois Hale, District 4

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS
 There were no comments from persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any agenda item
  except the Public Hearing.

C.APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1.Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on October 25, 2023,
 A motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Commissioner Galindo and seconded by Commissioner Rudd.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett Roberts and
  Lois Hale. All commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting notes.
 There was no rejection or noes.

2. Approval of the Minutes for the Special Meeting held on November 14, 2023
 A motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Commissioner Galindo and seconded by Commissioner Rudd.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett Roberts and
  Lois Hale. All commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting notes.
 There was no rejection or noes.

D. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. Vehicles parked from West Boulevard to Crenshaw Blvd at Manchester Boulevard: The vehicles in question at this
  location are blocking the pedestrian sidewalk. The Commission is looking for a solution that allows the sidewalk to
  have path accessible to all types of pedestrians at all time.
 The Parking and Traffic Department will provide a report at the next meeting for further discussion.

2. All informational links mentioned for the formation and responsibility of the Parking and Traffic Commission were
  provided to the entire commission. Chairman Hibler recommended that Commissioners consult Sections 2-107 through
  Section 2-107.8 of the Inglewood Municipal Code.

3. Information on Safe Routes to School document provided to Commissioner Rudd
 A request for presentation from the Commissioner was requested to understand the plan.

4. Termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program on 3rd Avenue from 102nd St to 104th St did not pass.
  Commission presented a report of the outcome. Please see the January agenda for reference.

E. NEW BUSINESS
1. Information on the Ordinance Designating City-Owned Parking Facilities as Parking Meter Zones and Establishing
  Special Event Parking Rates & fine for Parking Meter Zones. Please see the January agenda for reference.
 Commissioner Rudd requested a statistical report on shuttle and parking usage.

JANUARY 2024_PTC COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1 OF 2
   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, February 28, 2024 at 7:00 pm
  JANUARY 2024 MEETING MINUTES

F. PUBLIC HEARING
1. Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and the City line
  within District 11. Please see the January agenda for reference.
 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given regarding the rationale for the request.
 The resident did not receive any information to be included in the process prior to the implementation of the City's
  Residential Permit Program.
 Residents never had problems parking on the street before or after the stadium expansion.
 The Parking and Traffic Commission accepted the request and will continue with the voting process. A motion to accept
  was made by Commissioner Roberts and seconded by Commissioner Galindo.
 All five commissioners voted in favor of the application proceeding.

G. RESOLUTION
1. Staff report recommending that the Parking and Traffic Commission approve the resolution to terminate the Residential
  Permit Parking Program within District 9 at 102nd St and 7th Ave from Century Boulevard Local Access to 104th Street.
 The Parking and Transit Commission accepted the request and signed resolution. A motion to accept was made by
  Commissioner Galindo and seconded by Commissioner Rudd. All five commissioners voted in favor, accepted and
  signed the resolution.

H. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda.
 A resident raised the issue of the driver who abused the 20-minute loading zone at Manchester and Locust Street. This
  is causing the businessman to lose business. The resident was informed that the Parking and Traffic Department will
  support and monitor the locations to enforce parking laws.
 The resident requested a 4-way stop at Olive Street and Glasgow Avenue. The Commission took information and will
  investigate the matter.

I. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
 The commissioners thanked the City Clerk for attending the meeting.

J. ANNOUNCEMENTS
 It was announced that the next Traffic and Parking Commission meeting will be Wednesday, February 28, 2024 at 7:00
  p.m. m., 1st Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood, CA 90301

K. ADJOURNMENT
 The Parking and Traffic Commission meeting ended at 7:58 PM PST.

L. ATTACHMENT
 Attendance Sheet
 Resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within District 9 at 102nd Street and 7th Avenue from
  Century Boulevard Local Access to 104th Street

    CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Public Works Department
DATE:  February 28, 2024

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 6th Avenue from 104th
  Street to 108th Street within District 9

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to do the
following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program
  on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program. The program
is enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m.
to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities more
effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On October 10, 2023, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking on 6th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. There
is a count of thirty-eight (38) properties that are within the limit. Ten (10) valid signatures (one
signature per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting in twenty-eight percent (28%)
of all households on the block signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions.
On February 5, 2024, a notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary to attend the
February Traffic and Parking Commission meeting to express their views on the matter.

DISCUSSION:
The Residential Permit Parking District Program encourages residents to use their driveways to park
their vehicles, when available, so that those without driveways can park on the street. Therefore,
Public Works staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission to provide instructions on how to
proceed with the request by either:
1. Approving the request to start the voting process; or
2. Denying the request to end the processing of the petition.

A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 6th Avenue between 108th Street and 104th Street. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday February 28, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
9 on 6th Avenue between 108th Street and 104th Street would be warranted. If it is determined to be
warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la
terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 6th Avenue entre 108th
Street y 104th Street. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood,
este asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar
especificados:

  Miércoles 28 de Febrero de 2024 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente
la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad
para los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un
vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan
todos los espacios de estacionamiento disponibles en la calle. La Comisión de Tráfico y
Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en la
calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se justificaría la terminación de un permiso de estacionamiento
residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 6th Avenue entre 108th Street y 104th Street. Si se determina que
está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y
visitantes de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier
momento; incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea
expresar una opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento
de Obras Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
